subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers follow `agents.defaults.userTimezone` when it differs from the host timezone?
rationale: Current main has a clear source-proven gap, but the remaining fix changes shipped memory artifact naming semantics and may affect existing users' file organization.

options.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
options.body: Reuse the existing configured-timezone helpers for date, HHMM slug, and header output, then update tests and docs around the new artifact contract.

options.title: Keep host-local behavior
options.body: Close or narrow this as a docs/contract decision and make the hook documentation explicit that session-memory artifacts follow host or `TZ` local time.

options.title: Add a dedicated memory timezone setting
options.body: Introduce a new config surface only if maintainers want memory artifacts to differ from both host-local and `agents.defaults.userTimezone`.

recommendation.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
recommendation.body: Reuse the existing configured-timezone helpers for date, HHMM slug, and header output, then update tests and docs around the new artifact contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged the current host-local session-memory repair and is the strongest current-history route for deciding whether to change that behavior again.
